questions.q: What is a SageMaker JupyterLab space built on, per the AWS docs?
options: A Kubernetes cluster with many nodes
A single EC2 instance and a single EBS volume
An S3 bucket that runs code
A Glue job
questions.explain: A JupyterLab space uses one EC2 instance for compute and one EBS volume for storage, which holds your code, Git profile and environment variables.

questions.q: What happens to your files on the EBS volume when you switch the instance type?
options: They are deleted
They are copied to S3 automatically
They persist, because the volume is independent of the instance
They move to a different Region
questions.explain: The EBS volume persists independently of the instance's life, so switching instance types does not lose data.

questions.q: How did the lesson reduce the pandas memory of the 50,000-row table from 8.1 MB to 2.1 MB?
options: By deleting half the rows
By saving it as CSV
By using a bigger instance
By converting low-cardinality text columns to the category dtype
questions.explain: The region and plan columns repeat a few values, so the category dtype stores them compactly. The estimate of about 3.3 GB for 20 million rows is a floor, since pandas makes temporary copies.

questions.q: For customizing a Studio JupyterLab environment, what do the docs recommend?
options: Use a package manager rather than lifecycle configurations
Always write a lifecycle configuration script
Reinstall the operating system
Hard-code packages into the notebook cells only
questions.explain: Lifecycle configurations are more error-prone to debug and can increase startup time. Conda or pip on the persistent volume is easier, and pinning versions in Git makes the environment reproducible.

questions.q: Your data will not fit comfortably in the notebook instance's memory. What is the better response?
options: Buy the largest instance available
Sample nothing and hope for the best
Push the heavy work to Athena, Glue or a training job
Disable idle shutdown
questions.explain: Treat the notebook as a control room. Athena, Glue and managed training jobs can do heavy work without a giant notebook instance.
